chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Mudabbir from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever accuses his wife (of adultery) before consummating the marriage with her, he is lashed with the fixed punishment, and she remains his wife."

key_terms.قَذَفَ: Accused (specifically of adultery in the context of li'an)
key_terms.وَهِيَ امْرَأَتُهُ: And she is his wife (marital bond remains)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a husband who accuses his wife of adultery before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: In the context of Li'an (mutual imprecation) detailed in Surah An-Nur, this hadith clarifies the procedural nuance that if the accusation occurs prior to consummation, the husband receives the standard hadd punishment of eighty lashes without the need for the full four-fold oath and fifth curse sequence. Crucially, it establishes that the marital bond remains intact, distinguishing this scenario from cases where consummation might alter the legal consequences of the imprecation. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the status of the wife and the specific penal application during the pre-consummation phase of marriage.
